# ParamMute (previously PIP-KAG)

> ParamMute (Parametric Knowledge Muting through FFN Suppression) makes retrieval-augmented LLMs more faithful to retrieved evidence: it finds the mid-to-deep FFN layers that over-activate when a model ignores the context in favor of its parametric memory (Unfaithfulness-Associated FFNs, UA-FFNs), suppresses them, and calibrates the model toward external knowledge. Over vanilla RAG it raises average context recall by +6.17 on CoFaithfulQA and +54.63 on ConFiQA. Paper: "ParamMute: Suppressing Knowledge-Critical FFNs for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation" (Huang et al., NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2502.15543). Earlier arXiv versions were titled "PIP-KAG: Mitigating Knowledge Conflicts in Knowledge-Augmented Generation via Parametric Pruning".

- Problem: unfaithful generation in RAG, where the answer contradicts relevant, accurate retrieved context because the LLM falls back on its internal knowledge (knowledge conflict).
- Finding: unfaithful answers coincide with over-activation of a few mid-to-deep FFN layers (about 70%-90% relative depth); suppressing them makes unfaithful answers less likely.
- Method: (1) suppress UA-FFN activations with a coefficient lambda; (2) train a plug-and-play adaptation module with knowledge-augmented fine-tuning plus a max-margin knowledge-preference loss. The suppression strength can be adjusted at inference time to control reliance on parametric knowledge.
- Benchmark: CoFaithfulQA (released on Hugging Face as CoConflictQA), natural knowledge conflicts built from NQ, SQuAD, NewsQA, TriviaQA, SearchQA and HotpotQA; also evaluated on ConFiQA and FaithEval.
- Models: main backbone LLaMA3-8B-Instruct (8 of 32 FFN layers muted); the appendix extends to LLaMA3.2 (1B, 3B) and Qwen2.5 (0.5B-14B) Instruct.
